items.attribution: Louisa May Alcott · Little Women · Project Gutenberg
items.title: A Quiet Afternoon in Little Women

sentences.en: This scene comes from Little Women, a famous novel about family life, friendship, and the challenges of growing up.
sentences.zh: 这个场景来自《小妇人》，一部关于家庭生活、友谊和成长挑战的著名小说。

sentences.en: In this part of the story, a group of young people and children are spending a pleasant afternoon outdoors together.
sentences.zh: 在故事的这个部分，一群年轻人和孩子们一起在户外度过一个愉快的下午。

sentences.en: Ned, Frank, and the little girls join in a lively activity with energy, movement, and laughter.
sentences.zh: 内德、弗兰克和小女孩们加入了一项热闹的活动，充满活力、动作和笑声。

sentences.en: While they are busy, the three older people sit a little apart and talk together in a calm way.
sentences.zh: 当他们忙碌时，三位年长者稍微坐开一些，平静地一起交谈。

sentences.en: The younger ones are active and noisy, and their cheerful movement makes the outdoor scene feel lively.
sentences.zh: 年纪较小的人活跃又吵闹，他们欢快的动作让户外场景显得热闹。

sentences.en: The older ones, by contrast, seem to prefer a quieter and more serious conversation about their own interests.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，年纪较大的人似乎更喜欢安静而认真地谈论自己感兴趣的话题。

sentences.en: Miss Kate takes out her sketch again and begins to draw the people and things around her.
sentences.zh: 凯特小姐再次拿出她的速写本，开始画她周围的人和物。

sentences.en: Margaret watches her with interest, perhaps admiring how easily and carefully Miss Kate draws.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特饶有兴趣地看着她，也许在欣赏凯特小姐画得多么轻松而细致。

sentences.en: Mr. Brooke lies on the grass nearby with a book in his hand, but he is not really reading.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克先生躺在附近的草地上，手里拿着一本书，但他并不是真的在读书。

sentences.en: Instead, he seems to be lost in thought, perhaps listening to the talk around him.
sentences.zh: 相反，他似乎陷入了沉思，也许在听周围的谈话。

sentences.en: This small moment shows two kinds of activity happening in the same place at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这个小小的瞬间展现了同一地点、同一时间发生的两种活动。

sentences.en: The groups are together, yet each one has its own rhythm and mood, making the afternoon feel natural.
sentences.zh: 这些人群待在一起，但每一组都有自己的节奏和情绪，让这个下午显得自然。

items.attribution: Jane Austen · Pride and Prejudice · Project Gutenberg
items.title: A Playful Joke About Derbyshire in Pride and Prejudice
items.titleZh: 《傲慢与偏见》中关于德比郡的俏皮玩笑

sentences.en: In this scene from Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, an English county called Derbyshire is mentioned in a friendly conversation.
sentences.zh: 在简·奥斯汀《傲慢与偏见》的这个场景中，一次友好的谈话里提到了英格兰的德比郡。

sentences.en: Derbyshire is important because Pemberley, the large and beautiful country home of Mr. Darcy, is located there.
sentences.zh: 德比郡很重要，因为达西先生又大又美的乡间宅邸彭伯里就在那里。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Bennet has met Mr. Darcy before, and her feelings about him are still complicated and changing.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·班内特以前见过达西先生，她对他的感情仍然复杂且在变化。

sentences.en: She cannot hear the word Derbyshire without immediately thinking of Pemberley and its owner.
sentences.zh: 她一听到“德比郡”这个词，就会立刻想到彭伯里和它的主人。

sentences.en: The place has become closely connected in her mind with the proud, wealthy man she knows.
sentences.zh: 这个地方在她心里已经和她认识的那位骄傲而富有的男人紧密联系在一起。

sentences.en: To make light of these thoughts, Elizabeth decides to make a playful joke about visiting the area.
sentences.zh: 为了淡化这些想法，伊丽莎白决定就访问这个地区开一个俏皮的玩笑。

sentences.en: She suggests that she may enter his county safely and take a few small stones as souvenirs.
sentences.zh: 她提出自己也许可以安全地进入他的郡，并拿几块小石头当纪念品。

sentences.en: She also jokes that Mr. Darcy will probably never notice her harmless little theft.
sentences.zh: 她还开玩笑说，达西先生大概永远不会注意到她这无害的小小“偷窃”。

sentences.en: The phrase petrified spars refers to pieces of stone that look like fossils.
sentences.zh: “石化晶石”这个说法指的是看起来像化石的石块。

sentences.en: Her remark shows her quick sense of humour and her growing interest in Darcy's world.
sentences.zh: 她的话显示出她敏捷的幽默感，以及她对达西世界的兴趣日益增长。

sentences.en: At the same time, it suggests that she is not ready to admit her feelings openly.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这也表明她还不准备公开承认自己的感情。

sentences.en: In the end, a simple place name opens a clear window into Elizabeth's heart and mind, and the reader clearly sees her wit and confusion.
sentences.zh: 最终，一个简单的地名清楚地打开了通往伊丽莎白内心和思想的窗口，读者也能清楚看到她的机智和困惑。

items.title: Who Caught the Murderer? Victor Frankenstein's Shock
items.titleZh: 凶手被抓到了？弗兰肯斯坦的震惊

sentences.en: Victor Frankenstein is a young scientist in Mary Shelley's famous novel Frankenstein, which was published in 1818.
sentences.zh: 维克多·弗兰肯斯坦是玛丽·雪莱著名小说《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818年出版）中的一位年轻科学家。

sentences.en: After years of study, he learns how to give life to a body built from dead parts.
sentences.zh: 经过多年研究，他学会了如何让一具由死尸各部分拼成的躯体获得生命。

sentences.en: However, when the creature opens its eyes, Victor is horrified by its strange and ugly appearance.
sentences.zh: 然而，当这个生物睁开眼睛时，维克多被它怪异丑陋的外表吓坏了。

sentences.en: The creature runs away, and later it kills Victor's younger brother, William.
sentences.zh: 这个生物逃走了，后来它杀死了维克多年幼的弟弟威廉。

sentences.en: A kind servant named Justine is blamed for the crime and is sent to prison.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫贾斯汀的善良女仆被指控犯了这桩罪，并被送进监狱。

sentences.en: Victor knows who the real killer is, but he is too frightened to tell anyone the truth.
sentences.zh: 维克多知道真正的凶手是谁，但他太害怕了，不敢把真相告诉任何人。

sentences.en: One day, a man brings Victor the surprising news that the murderer has been discovered.
sentences.zh: 有一天，一个人给维克多带来了令人吃惊的消息：凶手已经被找到了。

sentences.en: Victor cannot believe his ears, and he cries out in shock, asking how anyone could possibly pursue such a powerful being.
sentences.zh: 维克多不敢相信自己的耳朵，他震惊地叫了出来，问怎么会有人能追得上这样一个强大的生物。

sentences.en: To him, chasing the creature is as hopeless as trying to overtake the wind or to stop a mountain stream with a straw.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，追赶这个生物就像想追上风，或者想用一根稻草堵住山间的溪流一样，毫无希望。

sentences.en: He also remembers seeing the creature the night before, walking completely free.
sentences.zh: 他还记得前一晚见过这个生物，它完全自由地走着。

sentences.en: So he is sure that the real killer is still out there, and that Justine is innocent.
sentences.zh: 因此他确信，真正的凶手仍然在外面，而贾斯汀是无辜的。

sentences.en: In the end, Justine is punished for a crime she did not commit, and Victor feels guilty for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 最终，贾斯汀因一项她并未犯下的罪行而受到惩罚，维克多余生都感到愧疚。

items.attribution: Arthur Conan Doyle · The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes · Project Gutenberg
items.title: Sherlock Holmes and the Strange Figure in the Dark
items.titleZh: 福尔摩斯与黑暗中的奇怪身影

sentences.en: Sherlock Holmes, the famous detective, and his friend Dr. Watson were travelling to an old country house at night.
sentences.zh: 著名侦探夏洛克·福尔摩斯和他的朋友沃森医生夜里正前往一座古老的乡间宅邸。

sentences.en: They had been asked to investigate a mysterious and frightening death that had happened in the house.
sentences.zh: 他们受托调查这所房子里发生的一起神秘而可怕的死亡事件。

sentences.en: The grounds around the building had been neglected for a long time, and the old park wall was in poor condition.
sentences.zh: 这栋建筑周围的庭院已经很久无人打理，旧庄园围墙也状况很差。

sentences.en: Several parts of the wall had fallen down, so Holmes and Watson found it easy to enter the grounds.
sentences.zh: 围墙有几处已经倒塌，因此福尔摩斯和沃森很容易就进入了庭院。

sentences.en: They moved carefully among the trees, trying not to make any noise, until they reached the lawn.
sentences.zh: 他们小心地穿过树林，尽量不发出声响，直到来到草坪。

sentences.en: After crossing the lawn, the two men walked slowly toward a window of the house.
sentences.zh: 穿过草坪后，两人慢慢朝房子的一扇窗户走去。

sentences.en: Suddenly, a strange figure darted out from a group of laurel bushes near them.
sentences.zh: 突然，一个奇怪的身影从他们附近的一丛月桂树中冲了出来。

sentences.en: In the dim light, it looked like a hideous and distorted child with strange, twisting limbs.
sentences.zh: 在昏暗的光线下，它看起来像一个丑陋而扭曲的孩子，四肢怪异地扭动着。

sentences.en: It threw itself onto the grass and moved its arms and legs in a wild, uncontrolled way.
sentences.zh: 它扑到草地上，四肢狂乱而不受控制地动着。

sentences.en: Then it ran swiftly across the lawn and disappeared into the darkness before they could react.
sentences.zh: 然后它迅速跑过草坪，在他们来得及反应之前消失在黑暗中。

sentences.en: Holmes and Watson stayed calm, but the strange sight made them even more alert.
sentences.zh: 福尔摩斯和沃森保持冷静，但这奇怪的景象让他们更加警觉。

sentences.en: They knew they had to continue their investigation, so they approached the window and entered the house.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己必须继续调查，于是靠近窗户，进入了房子。

items.attribution: H. G. Wells · The Time Machine · Project Gutenberg
items.title: The Ruined Library in the Future

sentences.en: The Time Traveller is exploring a distant future world with Weena, a gentle young woman he has befriended.
sentences.zh: 时间旅行者正和威娜一起探索一个遥远的未来世界；威娜是他结识的一位温柔的年轻女子。

sentences.en: He carries an iron mace in one hand and holds Weena with the other as they move through the buildings.
sentences.zh: 他一手拿着铁制权杖，另一手牵着威娜，两人穿过一栋栋建筑。

sentences.en: They leave a smaller gallery and enter a much larger hall that looks like an old military chapel.
sentences.zh: 他们离开一个较小的长廊，进入一个更大的大厅；这大厅看起来像一座古老的军中礼拜堂。

sentences.en: Torn flags seem to hang along its walls, but the Time Traveller soon recognises something different.
sentences.zh: 破损的旗帜似乎沿着墙壁悬挂，但时间旅行者很快认出情况并非如此。

sentences.en: The brown, burnt-looking rags are actually the remains of books that have fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 那些褐色、像被烧过的破布，其实是已经散架的书籍残骸。

sentences.en: No printed words are left, yet bent boards and cracked metal clasps show that these objects were once books.
sentences.zh: 书里没有留下任何印刷文字，但弯曲的木板和裂开的金属扣足以说明这些东西曾经是书。

sentences.en: A literary person might use this sight to warn people about the uselessness of human ambition.
sentences.zh: 有文学素养的人也许会借这一幕告诫人们：人类的雄心最终毫无用处。

sentences.en: The Time Traveller, however, feels most strongly the enormous amount of labour that produced these rotting books.
sentences.zh: 然而，时间旅行者感受最强烈的，是制造这些腐烂书籍所耗费的巨大劳动。

sentences.en: He admits that his own thoughts are quite personal and practical.
sentences.zh: 他承认，自己此刻的想法相当个人化，也很实际。

sentences.en: He thinks mainly of a famous scientific journal and the seventeen papers he once wrote on optics.
sentences.zh: 他主要想到一本著名的科学期刊，以及自己从前写的十七篇光学论文。

sentences.en: This moment suggests that the future has lost much of the knowledge and care that built its old civilisation.
sentences.zh: 这一刻表明，未来已经失去了许多曾建设旧文明的知识与关怀。

sentences.en: For the Time Traveller, the ruined library is a clear and troubling sign of a fallen civilisation.
sentences.zh: 对时间旅行者来说，这座废弃的图书馆是文明衰落的清晰而令人不安的标志。

items.attribution: Lewis Carroll · Alice's Adventures in Wonderland · Project Gutenberg
items.title: A Strange Tea Party in Wonderland

sentences.en: Alice is a curious young girl who follows a white rabbit into a strange world called Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝是一个好奇的小女孩，她跟着一只白兔进入了一个叫仙境的奇怪世界。

sentences.en: There she meets many unusual characters, including talking animals and people with very odd manners.
sentences.zh: 在那里，她遇到许多不寻常的角色，包括会说话的动物和举止古怪的人。

sentences.en: One day, she arrives at an outdoor tea party where the Mad Hatter and the March Hare are sitting together.
sentences.zh: 一天，她来到一个户外茶会，疯帽匠和三月兔正坐在一起。

sentences.en: They sit at a long table covered with teacups, but their behaviour seems very strange to Alice.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在一张摆满茶杯的长桌旁，但他们的行为在爱丽丝看来非常奇怪。

sentences.en: She cannot understand their jokes, their riddles, or the rude way they speak to each other.
sentences.zh: 她听不懂他们的笑话、谜语，也听不懂他们彼此说话时那种粗鲁的方式。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the Hatter shakes his head sadly and tells Alice that a recent quarrel was not his fault.
sentences.zh: 突然，帽匠伤心地摇摇头，告诉爱丽丝最近的一场争吵不是他的错。

sentences.en: He explains that he and the March Hare argued last March, just before the Hare went mad.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，他和三月兔去年三月争吵过，就在三月兔发疯之前。

sentences.en: While speaking, he points at the March Hare with the teaspoon he has been holding in his hand.
sentences.zh: 说话时，他用一直拿在手里的茶匙指着三月兔。

sentences.en: The argument took place at a grand concert organised by the Queen of Hearts, a powerful ruler.
sentences.zh: 那场争吵发生在红心皇后举办的一场盛大音乐会上；红心皇后是一位有权势的统治者。

sentences.en: At that event, the Hatter had to sing in front of everyone, and he clearly did not enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 在那场活动中，帽匠不得不在所有人面前唱歌，他显然并不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Alice listens carefully, but the story only makes her more confused about the two friends.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝仔细听着，但这个故事只让她对这两个朋友更加困惑。

sentences.en: Soon the tea party continues, and she realises that Wonderland is full of puzzling conversations.
sentences.zh: 很快，茶会继续进行，她意识到仙境充满了令人费解的对话。
